note: Batch 07: the 28 downloaded-but-uncarded SharePoint files (government, HySecure, HyID, HyWorks, pharma, VDI/TCO). Written from corpus/text/*.txt, every file read in full. Three findings shape these cards. (1) The HySecure 'Product-v2', '- Small' and '- Big' PDFs are NOT size variants: the base file is a full-portfolio 'Work from Anywhere' deck (HySecure, HyID, HyWorks, HyLabs, Nano, HyDesk), Small is a HySecure-only edition, and Big is Small plus the Gartner delivery-model slides, a company/customer appendix and web-proxy explanations - Big is the canonical HySecure edition. (2) Several documents carry the only Fortinet / Palo Alto / WireGuard / OpenVPN comparisons in the library (HySecure Product-v2 decks, Gateway as a Service, VDI vs VPN), which the 25 Sep content-gap test reported as missing - they are 2021-2024 and internal, but they exist. (3) The 2025-26 government decks reuse each other's slides heavily and contain internal contradictions (DSCI award 2024 vs 2025, 900+ vs 850+ customers, 90,000 vs 60,000 MFA users for the same bank, 'ISO 270001'); stale_risk names them so a rep does not quote the wrong one. Real customer names appear only in client_actual; brief, outcomes and use_for use descriptors.

cards.title: Accops HySecure ZTNA Gateway: Product Deck (Extended Edition, 2021)
cards.client: Call-centre and BYOD work-from-home deployments; appendix lists Japanese, Middle East and European government, healthcare and manufacturing customers
cards.client_actual: Kyoto University, Ibaraki Prefectural, Dubai Courts, City Pharmacy LLC, Zulekha Hospital, Al Zahra Hospital, Ahalia Medical Group, Fresenius Kabi, Kalle GmbH (customer logo list)
cards.key_problem: A layer-3 VPN bridges an unmanaged home PC into the corporate network, exposes data-centre subnets to any malware on it, and gives IT no control over data copy, internet use or which device the user logs in from.
key_outcomes: Three tunnel types in one gateway: L7 reverse proxy (clientless), L4 SPAN app tunnels (TLS 1.2), L3 Turbo tunnel (Noise protocol, ChaCha20-Poly1305) for VoIP
Turbo benchmark: 1,011 Mbps vs 825-881 Mbps for IPsec and 258 Mbps for OpenVPN; 8.9 vs 7.55 Mbps and 459 vs 244 KB/s download against a Palo Alto hardware appliance while running on a VM
Sizing per 8 vCPU VM: ~2,500-5,000 users (L7), ~2,000-3,000 (L4, 16 GB RAM), 2,000-5,000 CCU per node for Cisco / Palo Alto / Fortinet
Device binding by OS, CPU, HDD, motherboard and MAC IDs; host scan for AV, firewall, Windows updates; geo-location and impossible-travel reports
Four WFH architecture models for call-centre agents (gateway only, gateway + VDI, gateway + Nano bootable USB, all three) with pros, cons and a 14-control security comparison
Security of the appliance: CIS-hardened Linux, TLS 1.2/1.3, Qualys SSL A+, VAPT by a CERT-In empanelled lab, 12+ node HA clusters
Editions: Gold, Silver, Platinum; perpetual or subscription, concurrent or named users
cards.brief: The fullest of the three 2021 HySecure 'Product-v2' PDFs and the one to treat as canonical. It explains the gateway's three access modes (clientless L7, L4 SPAN app tunnels, L3 Turbo), why per-application tunnels hide the data centre where a layer-3 VPN exposes it, and the endpoint controls a VPN lacks: internet whitelisting without a web proxy, clipboard / print-screen / screen-share blocking, watermarking, device binding and host scan. It includes Turbo throughput and latency benchmarks against IPsec, OpenVPN and a Palo Alto appliance; Gartner-sourced delivery-model and BYOPC risk matrices; four call-centre WFH architectures with and without VDI and the Nano secure USB; how HySecure co-exists with an existing VPN and with cloud web proxies (including the SSH-bypass loophole in web-proxy agents); a three-table comparison of Accops L7/L4/L3 against WireGuard, OpenVPN and Cisco / Palo Alto / Fortinet covering deployment, security, cost and per-VM sizing; and a feature grid against Microsoft WVD, Citrix/VMware, Zscaler/McAfee, F5/Palo Alto and Okta/Cisco Duo. An appendix carries the 2021 company profile and customer logo list.
cards.use_for: A presales or architecture conversation about replacing a Cisco, Palo Alto or Fortinet VPN, sizing a HySecure gateway, VoIP / call-centre remote access, or explaining how ZTNA co-exists with an existing VPN or cloud web proxy. The closest thing the library has to a Fortinet comparison.
cards.stale_risk: Copyright 2021 on every slide. Company figures (600+ customers, 600,000+ users, 150+ team) are well below current material (900+ customers, 2M+ users). Competitor claims (Cisco Duo licensing, 'Zscaler SaaS only', 'Microsoft WVD') are 2021 positions - WVD is now Azure Virtual Desktop. Turbo sizing row reads '~5000-1000 users per VM', an obvious typo. For current product specs use the HySecure Datasheet V5 2026 (public).
cards.internal_reason: Marked 'Accops Confidential' on every slide; contains named competitor benchmarks and a customer logo list.
cards.needs_human: Near-duplicate family: 'Accops - HySecure - Product-v2.pdf' (Jul 2021, a different full-portfolio deck), '- Small.pdf' (Nov 2021, a subset of this one) and this '- Big.pdf' (Apr 2022 in SharePoint). Big contains everything in Small plus the Gartner matrices, company appendix and web-proxy notes, so Big is canonical and Small can be retired. Confirm, and confirm whether the .pptx twins in the same folder are the same editions.

cards.brief: Despite the file name, this is not just a HySecure deck: it is the 2021 'Work from Anywhere' company-plus-portfolio deck. The first half is company profile, recognitions, reference-customer logos, anonymised mini case studies and one page per product (HySecure, HyID, HyWorks with a Citrix/VMware feature table, HyLabs, Nano secure USB, HyDesk thin-client specs). The second half is the HySecure technology section shared with the Small/Big editions - SPAN app tunnels, Turbo benchmarks, Gartner delivery-model matrices, and the WireGuard / OpenVPN / Cisco / Palo Alto / Fortinet comparison tables - plus two 'Telco VPN' feature tables and a slide arguing a telco should not build its own VPN, which suggests it was prepared for a service-provider audience.
cards.use_for: A first meeting where the whole 2021 portfolio and the VPN comparison are both needed, or a telecom / managed-service-provider partner considering a hosted remote-access offering.

cards.title: Accops HySecure vs Cisco AnyConnect and Other VPNs (PDF, 2021)
cards.key_problem: A customer with a working VPN asks why they should replace it; the answer is what a VPN cannot do - contextual access, endpoint data control, built-in MFA and access without bridging the user's PC into the network.
key_outcomes: Cisco AnyConnect vs HySecure across protocol, access methods, deployment and security features
Cisco Duo licensed per named user; HySecure Gold includes MFA on concurrency - claimed ~70% MFA cost saving
Cisco: hardware appliance, single data centre per tunnel, no automatic DR switch; HySecure: virtual, multi-DC tunnels, auto DR failover
Turbo benchmarks vs IPsec, OpenVPN and a Palo Alto appliance
Why layer-3 VPNs are unsafe for BYOD: TCP-over-TCP overhead, route-table exposure, rogue apps using the tunnel
cards.brief: The PDF export of the 'HySecure vs Other VPNs' deck. It opens with three Cisco AnyConnect comparison slides (protocol, access methods, deployment, security features including Duo licensing, stealth client, device-ID binding, watermarking), then a generic 'other VPNs' table, the Accops-vs-WVD/Citrix/Zscaler/F5/Okta grid, Turbo benchmarks against IPsec, OpenVPN and a Palo Alto appliance, and a long technical appendix on VPN types (L2/L3/L4/reverse proxy), SPAN app-tunnel data flow, HySecure authentication, MFA and endpoint-control features, and the concerns with traditional VPNs.
cards.use_for: A prospect with Cisco AnyConnect or another VPN at renewal, or one who says a VPN plus Duo already covers remote access. Same deck as the PPTX battlecard; use whichever format the rep needs.
cards.stale_risk: Copyright 2021 on every slide (closing slide says 2019). Cisco Duo pricing and the 70% saving claim are five years old - verify before quoting. 'MS WVD' is now Azure Virtual Desktop.
cards.internal_reason: Marked 'Accops Confidential'; specific claims about a named competitor's licensing.
cards.needs_human: PDF twin of 'Accops - HySecure vs Other VPNs.pptx' (carded in batch-03). SAM collapses the two by file stem; one can be retired once the preferred format is chosen.

cards.title: AccOps Web VPN for eOffice: Solution Brief with National e-Governance Case (2020)
cards.client: India's national government IT agency, which hosts 100+ eOffice instances
cards.client_actual: NIC Delhi; also names CBDT, IDS, Indian Army, DRDO, IGCAR Kalpakkam, HPCL as government customers
cards.key_problem: Client-based VPNs for eOffice need software and certificates on every PC, become unmanageable above ~5,000 devices, let malware on personal PCs travel into the government network, and the incumbent vendor's web VPN did not support several eOffice modules.
key_outcomes: 525+ eOffice instances exist across central and state governments (context)
Pilot of 1,000 users deployed within a week; scaled to 50,000 named / 10,000 concurrent users within days of the lockdown
No endpoint touched by IT during rollout
Supports all eOffice modules on browser including Aadhaar signing and digital tokens, optimised with the eOffice team
Features: device lock-in, built-in OTP MFA, OWASP-based security, TLS 1.2+, geo-location policies, government LDAP, audit logs
cards.brief: A two-page solution brief. Page one frames the eOffice remote-access problem - a mission-mode NeGP project, web-based, but reachable from outside only through VPN clients that are hard to deploy at scale and risky on personal PCs - and positions AccOps HySecure Advanced as a clientless web VPN, with its feature list. Page two is the case study of the national e-governance IT agency: until 2019 it gave only senior officials VPN laptops, the incumbent's web VPN broke eOffice modules, a 1,000-user Accops pilot went live in a week, and at lockdown it scaled to 50,000 named and 10,000 concurrent users in days with zero endpoint work.
cards.use_for: A government or PSU buyer asking how to give eOffice (or any web application) secure remote access without VPN clients - a short, customer-shaped leave-behind.
cards.stale_risk: Copyright 2020 and uses the old 'AccOps' branding and '600+ customers & 600,000+ users'. The case has grown: 2025-26 decks cite 350,000-500,000 users at the same agency. Update numbers before sending.
cards.internal_reason: Names a government customer; no public URL confirmed. Customer-facing in style, so a refreshed version would be a strong public asset.
cards.needs_human: A candidate to refresh and publish as a government case study - content-gap item 8 (Q8) says there is no public government remote-access/VDI asset.
